name: tests-75pct-sh-diagnostic-bearing-recovered-syntax-trees
instr:
mvdan.cc/sh/v3 cannot currently carry parser recovery as a first-class result through every consumer. Make recovered input inspectable and renderable without allowing unsafe formatting, expansion, or command execution, while preserving valid-input behavior.

Return independent parse results with diagnostics and recovery associations in source order; a recovered-syntax diagnostic spans the zero-width position where syntax is missing (End equals Pos). Streaming must report each encountered diagnostic once, exclude unread input, and return the terminal error at the configured recovery limit. Keep recovery identities distinct, reachable, and associated through traversal, safe simplification, deterministic placeholder printing, and typed JSON round trips.

Strict printing must reject recovered input before writing. Every error-level diagnostic must prevent execution effects, including recovery nested in substitutions, redirections, functions, or background commands. `DiagnosticError` from `mvdan.cc/sh/v3/interp` carries every diagnostic in order. `RunResult(ctx, result) error` preserves `Runner.Run` behavior for valid results. `shfmt` and `gosh` report all recovered diagnostics deterministically without unsafe output or execution, preserving successful-input output and exit behavior.

`ExpandResult(input, env) ([]string, *syntax.ParseResult, error)` from `mvdan.cc/sh/v3/shell` withholds partial fields on diagnostic failure and otherwise matches existing expansion, splitting, envir
